'''Chennupati Jagadish''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AC}} (born 1957) is an [[Indian people|Indian]]-[[Australia]]n [[physicist]] and academic and the current president of the [[Australian Academy of Science]],<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/humble-beginnings-australian-science-leader|title=From humble beginnings to Australian science leader|date=2021-11-25|access-date=2026-03-16|website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref> and an Emeritus Professor of Physics at the [[Australian National University]] [[ANU Research School of Physics|Research School of Physics]]. He is head of the Semiconductor Optoelectronics and Nanotechnology Group which he established in 1990. He is also the Convener of the Australian Nanotechnology Network and Director of Australian National Fabrication Facility ACT Node.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Changes to the ANFF Ltd Board of Directors |url=https://anff.org.au/news/changes-to-the-anff-ltd-board-of-directors/ |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=Australian National Fabrication Facility Limited |language=en-AU}}</ref>

==Education==
Jagadish obtained his B.Sc. degree in physics from [[Acharya Nagarjuna University]] (VSR College, Tenali) in 1977, M.Sc. (Tech) in applied physics (with specialisation in electronics) from Andhra University in 1980 and M.Phil. and Ph.D. degrees in physics (semiconducting thin films) from the University of Delhi in 1982 and 1986, respectively.<ref name="Director">{{Cite web|url=https://physics.anu.edu.au/contact/people/profile.php?ID=106|title=Professor Chennupati Jagadish|website=Australian National University – Research School of Physics|language=en|access-date=2026-03-16}}</ref>

== Career ==
After completing his PhD in physics at the [[University of Delhi]], Jagadish worked at [[Sri Venkateswara College]], [[New Delhi]] as a lecturer in Physics and Electronics during 1985–1988. He was a post-doctoral fellow at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] Physics Department during 1988–1990. He moved to the [[Australian National University]] in 1990 to join the newly established Department of Electronic Materials Engineering in the Research School of Physics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://photonicssociety.org/newsletters/aug10/ServiceAward.html |title=IEEE PHOTONICS SOCIETY 2010 Distinguished Service Award Recipient: Chennupati Jagadish |date=2010 |access-date=31 December 2015 |work=Photonics Society |publisher=IEEE |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227064502/http://photonicssociety.org/newsletters/aug10/ServiceAward.html |archive-date=27 December 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has served as vice-president and Secretary for Physical Sciences of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] (2012–2016)<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.interacademies.net/File.aspx?id=26140|title=Australian Academy of Science Annual Report 2013-2014|publisher=Australian Academy of Science|year=2014|location=Canberra|pages=11|access-date=31 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304131139/http://www.interacademies.net/File.aspx?id=26140|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was elected President of the academy in May 2022, to serve a term of four years until May 2026.<ref name=":2" />

Jagadish has worked with overseas universities including the [[University of Oxford]], [[University of Tokyo]], [[IIT Delhi]], [[IIT Hyderabad]], [[University of Hyderabad]] and [[National Taiwan University]] where he holds honorary positions.<ref name="Director" />

He is an active member of IEEE Australian Material Research Society where he was President (2019–2022). He was also President, [[IEEE Photonics Society]] (2018–2019), and President, [[IEEE Nanotechnology Council]] (2008–2009), and regularly speaks at international conferences and meetings on Material Sciences, Photonics, Electronics, Semiconductors, Quantum Electronics, Physics, etc. He has also delivered plenary talks, and guest talks and organised several sessions in MRS, IEEE meetings around the globe.<ref name="Director"/>

He is now serving as Editor-in-Chief for [[Applied Physics Reviews]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://publishing.aip.org/about/news/aip-publishing-appoints-chennupati-jagadish-eic-of-apr/|title=AIP Publishing Appoints Professor Chennupati Jagadish, Ph.D., as the new Editor-in-Chief of Applied Physics Reviews|website=AIP Publishing LLC|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref> (January 2020 – present). Before joining APR, he served as Editor-in-Chief for Progress in [[Quantum Electronics]] (2016–2019), and as Co-Editor-in-Chief for the [[International Journal of High Speed Electronics and Systems]] (2014–2019). He also holds Editor position for various journals including IEEE Electron Device Letters (2008–2014), [Journal of Semiconductor Technology and Science (2009–present), Springer Series in Material Science, (2009–present),  Springer Series in Nanooptics and Nanophotonics (2009–present), Elsevier Series in Semiconductors and Semimetals (2010–present), Light: Science and Applications of Nature Publishing Group, (2014–2019). He is the member of the editorial board for more than 20 other journals, including [[ACS Nano]], IEEE Photonics Journal, IEEE Nanotechnology Magazine, [[Physica Status Solidi]]: Rapid Res. Lett., Solid State Electronics, Etc.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Chennupati |first=Jagadish |title=JC CV |url=https://physics.anu.edu.au/contact/people/download_cv.php?PeopleID=106}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Dr. Chennupati Jagadish Bio - IEEE Photonics Society |url=https://www.photonicssociety.org/dr-chennupati-jagadish-bio |access-date=2020-04-28 |website=www.photonicssociety.org |language=en-gb}}</ref>

== Social services ==
Jagadish and his wife Vidya have launched The Chennupati and Vidya Jagadish Endowment to support students and researchers from developing countries to visit [[Australian National University]]'s [[ANU Research School of Physics|Research School of Physics]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.labonline.com.au/content/lab-business/news/endowment-fund-to-support-scientists-from-the-developing-world-1303217325|title=Endowment fund to support scientists from the developing world|access-date=2026-03-16|website=LabOnline|date=2016-12-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/technology/anu-nanotechnology-scientist-chennupati-jagadish-endowment-fund-supporting-internships-20160511-gos663.html|title=ANU nanotechnology scientist Chennupati Jagadish endowment fund supporting internships|access-date=2026-03-16|last=Macdonald|first=Emma|date=2016-05-16|work=The Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.anu.edu.au/news/all-news/anu-launches-program-for-india%E2%80%99s-up-and-coming-researchers|title=ANU launches program for India's up-and-coming researchers|access-date=2026-03-16|date=2018-08-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180823064403/http://www.anu.edu.au/news/all-news/anu-launches-program-for-india%E2%80%99s-up-and-coming-researchers|archive-date=2018-08-23|url-status=dead|website=Australian National University}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Jagadish has received many awards and honours including being elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2003,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2003&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> and a Fellow The Optical Society in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Director&nbsp;(Research&nbsp;Services&nbsp;Division) |title=Professor Chennupati Jagadish |url=https://researchers.anu.edu.au/researchers/jagadish-c#biography |access-date=2024-07-12 |website=researchers.anu.edu.au |language=en-US}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Federation Fellowship]] (2004–2009) and [[Australian Laureate Fellowship|Laureate Fellowship]] (2009–2014) by the [[Australian Research Council]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.industry.gov.au/ministerarchive2011/carr/Speeches/Pages/AUSTRALIANLAUREATEFELLOWSHIPS.html|title=Australian Laureate Fellowships Announcement|access-date=25 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151227005602/http://archive.industry.gov.au/ministerarchive2011/carr/Speeches/Pages/AUSTRALIANLAUREATEFELLOWSHIPS.html|archive-date=27 December 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>
He was awarded the 2013 [[Walter Boas Medal]] from the [[Australian Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aip.org.au/medals-awards-and-prizes/walter-boas-medal/|title=Walter Boas Medal|publisher=Australian Institute of Physics|access-date=10 February 2020|archive-date=21 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921012931/https://aip.org.au/medals-awards-and-prizes/walter-boas-medal/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2015, he received both the IEEE [[Pioneer Award in Nanotechnology]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NTC Award Winners Announced |url=http://sites.ieee.org/nanotech/2015-ntc-award-winners-announced/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220083717/http://sites.ieee.org/nanotech/2015-ntc-award-winners-announced/ |archive-date=2016-02-20 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=IEEE}}</ref> and the IEEE Photonics Society Engineering Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015 |title=2015 IEEE Photonics Society Engineering Achievement Award: Chennupati Jagadish, Australian National University |url=http://photonicssociety.org/sites/default/files/EA%20Recipient_2.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127190712/http://photonicssociety.org/sites/default/files/EA%20Recipient_2.pdf |archive-date=2016-01-27 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=IEEE Photonics Society}}</ref> In 2016, he received the Nick Holonyak, Jr. Award, "For pioneering and sustained contributions to quantum-well, quantum-dot and nanowire optoelectronic devices and their integration."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Director&nbsp;(Research&nbsp;Services&nbsp;Division) |title=Professor Chennupati Jagadish |url=https://researchers.anu.edu.au/researchers/jagadish-c#biography |access-date=2024-07-12 |website=researchers.anu.edu.au |language=en-US}}</ref>

Jagadish was appointed a Companion of the [[Order of Australia]] for eminent services to physics and engineering in the [[Australia Day Honours]] 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/act-news/australia-day-honour-for-dedicated-indian-academic-20160121-gmayly|title=Australia Day Honours 2016: Indian academic Chennupati Jagadish a pioneer in nanotechnology|last=Macdonald|first=Emma|date=25 January 2016|work=Brisbane Times|access-date=25 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2016/jan/26/neurotechnologist-chennupati-jagadish-science-is-fun-for-me|title=Neurotechnologist Chennupati Jagadish: 'science is fun for me'|last=Brereton|first=Adam|date=26 January 2016|work=The Guardian|access-date=25 January 2016}}</ref> and received the 2018 UNESCO medal for his contributions to nanoscience and nanotechnologies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chennupati Jagadish wins UNESCO Medal for nanotech |url=https://www.atse.org.au/news-and-events/article/chennupati-jagadish-wins-unesco-medal-for-nanotech/ |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=Australian Academy of Technology & Engineering |language=en|date=2018-11-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329083247/https://www.atse.org.au/news-and-events/article/chennupati-jagadish-wins-unesco-medal-for-nanotech/|archive-date=2020-03-29|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2019, he received the [[Thomas Ranken Lyle Medal]] from the [[Australian Academy of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/opportunities-scientists/recognition/honorific-awards/honorific-awardees/2019-awardees#lyle|title=2019 Thomas ranken Lyle Medal|publisher=Australian Academy of Science|access-date=10 February 2020}}</ref> and the Beattie Steel Medal, presented by the Australia and New Zealand Optical Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ANZOS - Australia and New Zealand Optical Society - W.H. (Beattie) Steel Medal |url=https://optics.org.au/W.H.(Beattie)-Steel-Medal |access-date=2022-06-02 |website=optics.org.au |archive-date=29 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629225803/https://optics.org.au/W.H.(Beattie)-Steel-Medal |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2020, he was elected an international member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to nanotechnology for optoelectronic devices.
In 2022, he was elected as an international fellow of the UK's [[Royal Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.anu.edu.au/news/all-news/anu-professor-elected-to-royal-academy-of-engineering| title=ANU Professor Elected to Royal Academy of Engineering }}</ref>
In 2023, the [[President of India]] conferred on Jagadish the [[Pravasi Bharatiya Samman]] Award for his "contributions to science and technology and education". This is the highest honour given to overseas Indians by the Government of India.<ref name="Pravasi Bharatiya Samman award">{{cite news |title='Deeply honoured': 2023 Pravasi Bharatiya Samman award recipient Prof Jagadish|url=https://www.sbs.com.au/language/hindi/en/podcast-episode/australia-based-prof-chennupati-bags-pravasi-bharatiya-samman-award-this-year/qh3h4qamz |access-date=16 June 2023 |publisher=SBS |date=17 January 2023}}</ref>

He was made a Foreign Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows update—November 2023 |url=https://www.science.org.au/academy-newsletter/november-2023-177/fellows-update |access-date=2024-06-27 |website=Australian Academy of Science}}</ref> and elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]] in 2024<ref>{{Cite web |title=Society welcomes new Members and Fellows: April 2024 |url=https://royalsoc.org.au/blog/society-welcomes-new-members-and-fellows-april-2024 |access-date=2024-06-13 |website=The Royal Society of NSW}}</ref> and of the [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Royal Society]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>

He has received honorary doctorates from the [[University of Surrey]] (2024)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary graduates |url=https://www.surrey.ac.uk/about/people/honorary-graduates |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=University of Surrey}}</ref> and [[Nottingham Trent University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary graduates |url=https://www.ntu.ac.uk/alumni/alumni-stories/honorary-graduates |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=Nottingham Trent University |language=en}}</ref>

He received the 2026 [[IEEE Photonics Award]], "for contributions to compound semiconductor nanotechnology for optoelectronic devices and impact on the Photonics community".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://corporate-awards.ieee.org/recipient/chennupati-jagadish/ |title=Chennupati Jagadish – 2026 IEEE Photonics Award |website=[[IEEE Awards]] |access-date=November 5, 2026 }}</ref>
